newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline edges higher, watches France, API's.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline edges higher, watches France, API's.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices edged higher on Tuesday, tracking some of crude's late gains on Monday and a slightly bullish response to the ongoing strike at three Elf refineries in France, traders said.
But physical action was very quiet as crude retraced some gains and there were no visible signs of French buying that surfaced on Monday, they said.
Eurograde barges were bid at $216 and offered at $218 fob ARA by early afternoon, traders said, against late Monday levels of $214/$216.
"On motor gasoline, it's a quiet market today with people waiting for the APIs," said one barge trader.
Recent European gasoline exports to the U.S. Atlantic Coast may start to show up in the weekly inventory data, he said.
He said the French strikes were not creating big waves in the barge market but "it certainly supports sentiment."
Striking Elf Aquitaine refinery workers failed to get their full demands ahead of the scheduled talks at 1400 GMT with managers.
One senior union official said Elf refused an offer to unblock deliveries from the refineries in return for a pledge to negotiate on all the strikers' demands.
The strike crippling a quarter of French refinery production at three Elf plants entered its sixth day on Tuesday
